answer: An AI-agent marketplace can grant one vote per public key backed by 100 credits locked for a 30-day ballot. Its contract binds each deposit to one key until voting closes, so aliases named summit, tundra, and nebula require separate deposits. Each additional fake voter ties up another 100 credits. At a 12% annual capital cost, that imposes about 0.99 credits in marginal financing cost per fake voter per ballot, even when the principal is returned.
